subject: Capacity cartography & cushion proposal for Centauri committed fleet
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Zhao <eli@centauri.ai>, Maya Reddy <maya@centauri.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity cartography & cushion proposal for Centauri committed fleet

Eli / Maya —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached are two artifacts I promised: a token-level snapshot we pulled from your trial traffic (centauri_tokens_snapshot.csv) and an initial safety-cushion workbook (safety_cushion_model.xlsx). High-level summary below — want to confirm a few assumptions before we lock the commit sizing: 

Key findings (short):
- Baseline matched traffic median: ~1.1k tokens/sec (aggregate across 3 endpoints) during business hours.
- 95th percentile concurrency spikes push short-lived demand to ~3.8k tokens/sec (bursts 30–90s).
- Model variants: m-latent (lower latency / higher cost) used for web tier; m-economy (quantized) for async batch.

Recommendations for a committed slab (first-pass):
1) Commit slab sized for 5k tokens/sec sustained with ability to burst to 12k for short windows — this yields ~2.4x 95th percentile headroom.
2) Configure an onramp policy to route non-critical batch to m-economy during peak to preserve p95 latency for web.
3) Reserve a warm KV-cache pool and a 1-node overflow (burst) cushion for cold-start-heavy launches.

Open questions for you:
- Do you expect a product launch within the next 90 days that would change the burst profile (e.g., marketing-driven spikes)?
- Any hard p95 latency targets for the web flows we should encode in the SLO (currently assumed p95 <= 350ms for m-latent)?

Next steps: if these assumptions look right, we’ll share a compute->tokens mapping and a flash runbook mapping (ops playbook) and propose a 6-month commit with a 20% overprovision buffer for the first 8 weeks.

Attachments: centauri_tokens_snapshot.csv (sampled traffic), safety_cushion_model.xlsx (modelled scenarios)

—
Logan Wright
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Eli Zhao <eli@centauri.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Maya Reddy <maya@centauri.ai>
Cc: Centauri Procurement <procurement@centauri.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity cartography & cushion proposal for Centauri committed fleet

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points before we commit:

- Launch timing: we have a soft launch planned in mid-May (targeted PR + feature flag rollouts) which could double peak requests for 48–72 hours. So short spikes are likely higher than historical trial traffic.
- p95 latency: product requires p95 <= 300ms for the web inference route. Anything above that and we’ll degrade UX.
- Cost sensitivity: Procurement flagged that a 2.4x multiplier on 95th might be too generous from a cost perspective; they asked whether a dynamic fallback (regional overflow / queued async) could reduce the committed slab.

Can your team model a launch spike scenario (2x sustained for 72h, with sustained 20% of traffic at highest fidelity) and show the delta in required GPUs / token budget? Also please include the failure-safe: if we hit the burst cap, what observable & throttling experience will our users see?

—
Eli Zhao
Head of Product
Centauri.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Zhao <eli@centauri.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Maya Reddy <maya@centauri.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity cartography & cushion proposal for Centauri committed fleet

Eli —

Appreciate the launch window note. I modeled three discrete scenarios and attached the condensed math (tps-model-v2.pdf) and pushed the full workbook to our shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/centauri/capacity-cartography/v2 

Highlights from the models (short):
- Scenario A (base): sustain 5k tps -> maps to 4 x A40-equivalent nodes (in our probed kernel profile), p95 ~ 280–320ms depending on mix.
- Scenario B (2x launch spike sustained 72h): effective demand ~10k tps; recommended commit slab = 8 x A40 nodes with 1 burst node; ops ramping + KV-warm reduces tail by ~18% vs cold.
- Scenario C (cost-constrained hybrid): commit 4 nodes, auto-fallback to quantized m-economy for 35% of requests when utilization > 75% — predicts p95 degrade to ~360–420ms for those degraded paths, web SLO violated unless preferred routing preserves web tier.

Suggested safety/playbook action:
1) For mid-May launch, set temporary burst-cap (paid burst pool) to match Scenario B for 72h, with automatic rollback to Scenario A slab after 96h.
2) Add a routing rule: preserve the web inference (route tag = web) to m-latent until 85% utilization, only then allow fallback to m-economy for non-critical flows.
3) Instrument synthetic checks at 30s frequency; if p95 crosses 320ms for 3 consecutive checks, enable emergency routing to standby region (we can add a 1-node standby in us-west with cross-region routing).

Attached: tps-model-v2.pdf (math), I uploaded the full working MAP to the drive and started a draft MAP doc (centauri_MAP.docx) with responsibilities.

I’ll be available Wed afternoon if you want to walk the numbers live.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Eli / team —

Thanks Karthik — that modeling is exactly what Procurement and Product asked for. Quick alignment and proposed decision points so we can move to a draft SOW: 

Agreed actions:
- Commit: start with Scenario A (4 nodes) + a 72h paid burst to Scenario B (add 4 nodes + 1 burst node) to cover the mid-May launch. Procurement is comfortable with a timeboxed burst vs permanent overcommit.
- SLO: formalize web p95 target at 300ms. Karthik to author the SLO definition (synthetic probes, sampling, and exclusion rules for retries).
- Ops: we’ll implement the routing rule to preserve web until 85% utilization. Naomi will draft the cross-region fallback play for emergency.
- Contract ask: include a one-time burst credit to cover the paid burst window and a 30-day rollback review clause.

Next steps: I’ll share a one-page mutual action plan and the SOW language for the commit sizing by tomorrow EOD. Please review and flag any changes.

Attachments referenced: centauri_MAP.docx (draft MAP)

—
Logan Wright
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
